name: colorsnap
idea: ColorSnap is a free, browser-only color palette extractor that lets designers and developers instantly pull hex codes, RGB values, and export-ready code (CSS, SCSS, Tailwind, JSON) from any uploaded image — no signup, no server, completely private.
why_trending: Color palette tools are perennially high-traffic among designers; Coolors.co ranks in the top 10k globally and earns premium subscriptions at $3/month. In 2026, the surge in AI-generated imagery and brand-kit creation for creator-economy products has spiked searches for 'extract colors from image' and 'image color palette generator' per Google Trends signals found in May 2026 research.
why_profitable: Coolors Premium charges $3/month; Adobe Color has Pro features. A free tool monetizes through high-CPM display ads (design/dev audience at $4–9 CPM), a one-time 'Pro unlock' for bulk export and saved palettes ($4.99), and affiliate links to design tools like Figma, Canva Pro, and Adobe.
why_easy: 100% static HTML/CSS/JS — the HTML5 Canvas API reads pixel data client-side with no server calls. Three built-in extraction algorithms (Median Cut, K-Means, Dominant Frequency) run entirely in the browser. Six export formats (CSS variables, SCSS, Tailwind config, HEX, RGB, JSON) are pure string generation. Zero npm, zero build step, deployable to GitHub Pages instantly.
